title: Distance and Similarity
subtopics: Choosing a distance metric for a task
learning_outcomes: Explain distance and similarity and accurately refer to at least two syllabus subtopics.
Apply the main idea of distance and similarity to a small example, trace, calculation, or scenario.
Identify one important assumption or failure mode and describe how to check it.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study distance and similarity in the context of mathematical foundations. You will connect the PDF subtopics to a small example and practice describing what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Distance and Similarity matters because it affects how data is collected, represented, analyzed, interpreted, or used in a decision. Check the task and assumptions before choosing a method.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Mathematics helps describe data, measure uncertainty, represent relationships, and optimize model parameters. Interpret notation and units rather than memorizing formulas alone.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: 1. Restate the question addressed by distance and similarity. 2. Identify the input data, intended output, and assumptions. 3. Predict what the small example should show before reading its output. 4. Change one input or assumption, compare the result, and document what remains uncertain.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the provided synthetic input, rerun or retrace the example, and change one value at a time. Do not use personal records, credentials, or data you are not authorized to access.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Keep the question, data grain, units, and assumptions explicit. If a result differs, inspect the input and steps in order. Avoid turning an observed association into a causal claim, treating a sample as the population, or assuming a small demonstration guarantees production behavior. The dot product multiplies corresponding vector values and sums the products.

task_acceptance_criteria: Refer accurately to the topic and its syllabus subtopics.

Document at least one assumption, limitation, data-quality issue, or evaluation check.
hints: Write down the input, expected result, units, and assumptions first.
Change only one condition when testing a revised example.
Ask whether the data and method represent the real decision; do not infer causality or production readiness from a toy example.
